mechanism: The retail inventories-to-sales ratio rises when stock accumulates faster than sales, a sign of softening demand that can precede order and production cuts; the prior is countercyclical (reduce SPY when the ratio is high).
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time RETAILIRSA vintages) there is no winner: the archive starts 2013-07-31 and leaves 47 training months, fewer than the 60 required. On today's revised data (hindsight) the rule selected on in-sample data uses level at L6 (procyclical) with test-period Sharpe 0.82 versus buy-and-hold 0.96.
caveats: There is no result on data as known at the time: the vintage archive is too short for the training window. The as-revised-today result uses today's corrected values and is hindsight.
The hindsight rule is procyclical, opposite to the countercyclical prior.
The strategy is search-selected and needs fresh holdout validation.
narrative_summary: Retail inventories relative to sales are tested as a demand-softness signal for SPY allocation; the real-time archive is too short to rank the pair.

known_stress_episodes.label: Global Financial Crisis
known_stress_episodes.note: Sales collapsed faster than inventories; the ratio spiked.

known_stress_episodes.label: COVID shock
known_stress_episodes.note: Ratio spiked as stores closed, then fell to record lows as sales rebounded.
